deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page). Let mu = a+bi be an odd Gaussian integer with norm nu = a^2+b^2. X is the set of the nu-1 residues mod mu that are not divisible by mu. Note that for composite mu this means all nonzero residues, not only the units. Because mu is odd, psi, i*psi, -psi and -i*psi are pairwise incongruent for psi not 0 mod mu: (1-i)psi ≡ 0 or 2psi ≡ 0 would force psi ≡ 0. So X splits into four 'zusammengehörige Viertelsysteme' x, x' ≡ ix, x'' ≡ -x, x''' ≡ -ix, each of size (nu-1)/4.

This page, step by step.

(1) Multiplying by m. Let m be coprime to mu. Then psi -> m*psi permutes X. It also commutes with multiplication by i. Hence mx, mx', mx'', mx''' (taking the representatives that lie in X) form another decomposition of X into associated quarter systems. Gauss says 'the proof is easy'. So X is decomposed in two ways.

(2) Intersection counts. Define lambda_j = |mx ∩ x^(j)| for j = 0..3. Since mx^(k) = i^k*mx and x^(j+k) = i^k*x^(j), multiplication by i^k gives |mx^(k) ∩ x^(j+k)| = lambda_j (indices mod 4). This is Gauss's statement 'x' mit mx' ... lambda Glieder; x'' mit mx' ... lambda' Glieder u.s.w.'

(3) The character. Define epsilon ≡ lambda_1 + 2*lambda_2 + 3*lambda_3 (mod 4), with epsilon in {0,1,2,3}.

(4) Claim: epsilon does not depend on the choice of the quarter system x.

(5) First, abandoned approach. Change x in a single element: replace phi by i^delta*phi with delta in {1,2,3}. This is the elementary-exchange argument; Gauss drops it.

(6) Notation. Pi(psi) = j if psi lies (up to congruence) in x^(j). Then:
- I: Pi(i*psi) ≡ 1 + Pi(psi) (mod 4).
- II: i^(-Pi(psi))*psi lies in x.
- III: summing over phi in x, Sum Pi(m*phi) ≡ epsilon (mod 4). Indeed m*phi lies in x^(j) for exactly lambda_j values of phi.

(7) Second approach, carried out on the next page. Let k = {f, f', f'', ...} be any other quarter system, with k' ≡ ik, k'' ≡ -k, k''' ≡ -ik. Order its elements so that f is associated to phi, f' to phi', and so on. Let P be the index function for the k-decomposition, playing the role Pi plays for x. The goal (next page) is Sum P(mf) ≡ Sum Pi(m*phi) (mod 4). The argument:
- P(mf) - P(m*phi) ≡ P(f) - P(phi), so the first difference ≡ -Sum P(phi).
- P(m*phi) - Pi(m*phi) ≡ P(i^(-Pi(m*phi))*m*phi).
- The elements i^(-Pi(m*phi))*m*phi run through x again (a permutation), so the second difference ≡ Sum P(phi).
- The total is 0 mod 4.

(8) Meaning (my addition, not stated on the page). For prime mu, i^epsilon is the quartic residue symbol [m/mu] ≡ m^((nu-1)/4) (mod mu). This is the quartic Gauss lemma. For composite odd mu, epsilon defines a 'character' of m modulo mu, i.e. a quartic Jacobi-type symbol defined via a lemma that uses all nonzero residues.
errors: Formula III as written (and as transcribed) reads Sum Pi(phi) ≡ epsilon over phi in x. Over x every Pi(phi) = 0, so this must be Sum Pi(m*phi) ≡ epsilon. The next page indeed uses Sum Pi(m*phi). It is a slip of the pen or a misreading.
The sentence 'Im letzten Fall kann dies so ge-[schehen]' is interrupted by a struck line, so the syntax is broken. There is no mathematical error.
The single-element-exchange proof (k differs from x in one element phi -> i^delta*phi) is started and then abandoned in favour of the general argument. Both approaches would work.

The claim that mx, mx', mx'', mx''' form associated quarter systems is asserted with 'Der Beweis ist leicht zu führen'. It is correct, because m is invertible mod mu and multiplication by m commutes with multiplication by i. It is valid even for composite mu with X = all nonzero residues.

results.what: Decomposition of the nonzero residues mod an odd Gaussian integer into four associated quarter systems, and invariance of the decomposition under multiplication by m coprime to mu.
results.modern_name: Choice of a set of representatives of (Z[i]/mu \ {0}) modulo the action of the unit group <i> (a 'quarter system', analogue of a half system)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (biquadratic residue theory); half-system analogue Gauss 1808

results.what: epsilon ≡ lambda_1 + 2*lambda_2 + 3*lambda_3 = Sum_{phi in x} Pi(m*phi) (mod 4) is independent of the choice of quarter system; i^epsilon gives the biquadratic character of m mod mu.
results.modern_name: Gauss's lemma for quartic residues (quartic residue symbol via a quarter system)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, Werke II); also used by Eisenstein (1844)

results.what: Extension of this lemma-type definition to composite odd moduli mu, counting all nonzero residues, not just units.
results.modern_name: Gauss-lemma definition of the quartic Jacobi symbol (analogue of Schering's 1876 extension of Gauss's lemma to the Jacobi symbol)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi symbol: Jacobi 1837; Gauss-lemma version for composite moduli: Schering 1876; quartic analogue: unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The quartic Gauss lemma is known to be in Gauss's Nachlass (printed in Werke II). The deliberate generalization to composite odd Gaussian moduli, with a full invariance proof, anticipates Schering-type extensions. It is notable but probably already documented in Werke II.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import I, expand; m=1+I; x=[1,1+I]; reps={0:[1,1+I],1:[I,-1+I],2:[-1,-1-I],3:[-I,1-I]}  # mu=3: m*1=1+I in x (Pi=0), m*(1+I)=2I ≡ -I mod 3 in x''' (Pi=3); epsilon=3
checkable.asserts: For mu=3 (nu=9), m=1+i, the quarter system gives epsilon=3.
Euler criterion check: (1+i)^((9-1)/4) = (1+i)^2 = 2i ≡ -i = i^3 (mod 3). This agrees with epsilon=3.

checkable.sympy: for prime mu (e.g. mu=3+2*I, nu=13) and m coprime to mu: i**epsilon ≡ m**((nu-1)/4) mod mu, with epsilon = sum over a quarter system x of Pi(m*phi) mod 4
checkable.asserts: The quartic Gauss lemma: the character equals the quartic residue symbol.

checkable.sympy: for random quarter systems x1, x2 mod an odd Gaussian mu (e.g. mu=3*(3+2*I)) and m coprime to mu: eps(x1,m) == eps(x2,m)
checkable.asserts: epsilon is independent of the choice of quarter system, also for composite mu with X = all nonzero residues.

checkable.sympy: for composite odd mu = pi1*pi2: i**eps(m,mu) == [m/pi1]_4 * [m/pi2]_4
checkable.asserts: Conjectural, not on this page: the composite-modulus character is multiplicative in mu, i.e. it is the quartic Jacobi symbol.

transcription_corrections: 'so bildeten die Producte' should read 'so bilden die Producte'.
'die mit jenem zusammengehören' is likely 'die mit jenen zusammengehören'.
Formula III: the intended reading is Sum Pi(m*phi) ≡ epsilon (mod 4). The 'm' is missing either in the manuscript or in the transcription.
'Es sei nun [-k-] ein anderes Viertelsystem': k is written (overwritten or corrected), not simply deleted. The following text uses k, k', k'', k'''.
The 'Charakteristik rho' at the bottom is the symbol written P on the next page.
The red marginal 'Im' (left) is an editorial mark. There is also a faint, illegible marginal note at the right edge near the definition of epsilon.
